content:
I have to admit, my DIY iPhone camera rig looks a bit ridiculous — but it's actually made shooting photos and video on my phone far more practical, and a lot more fun.

What started as a quick fix to get a single shot done has turned into something I find myself reaching for way more than I expected…

One of the biggest divides in the compact camera world has always been whether you actually need a viewfinder. Old-school photographers would argue endlessly about the merits of an electronic viewfinder (EVF) versus an optical one, but EVFs are now so good that almost no one bothers debating the point anymore.

That said, whether optical or electronic, a viewfinder offers real, tangible benefits over composing on the rear screen — especially when you're shooting in harsh sunlight. Even at full brightness, it can be nearly impossible to see the image clearly in bright sun, and you may also have to deal with screen glare.

In London this isn't a huge issue for me, but we've had record-breaking heatwaves this summer and, honestly, I feel like the last time I saw a cloud or a drop of rain was about thirty years ago.

For me, though, the reason goes beyond that. I've found that looking at the world through the viewfinder, framed by the box around it, versus looking at the world around the frame, gives you a fundamentally different psychological experience. Sometimes, it's exactly that difference that makes me pick up a dedicated camera over my iPhone.

A few years ago, when I was choosing a camcorder, the Blackmagic Pocket Cinema Camera 4K was pretty much the obvious pick for most people, but the lack of a viewfinder put me off slightly. In the end I decided it wasn't a big deal for me, because I mostly shoot indoors, and when I'm out, attaching a large screen with a sun hood basically solves most of the problem.

But sometimes I want something more portable than a whole monitor rig, so I found a simple accessory that's really handy out in the field. It's a two-in-one sun hood and magnifying viewfinder that magnetically clips onto the rear screen, effectively giving you an optical viewfinder.

I had an upcoming shoot where I needed to film with both the BMPCC 4K and the iPhone 16 Pro Max. I did a quick test on set and found the viewfinder accessory incredibly useful. Since the screens on the BMPCC 4K and the iPhone are roughly the same size, I wondered if I could use this thing with the iPhone.

Obviously, the iPhone has no magnet to attach it, but the iPhone is light enough that I can just hold it in place with my hand against the magnifier without any problem. What surprised me was how well it actually works, especially when I use the Camera Control button as a shutter.

Since then, I've used this thing in every situation — partly for the real practical benefit of being able to see the screen better in bright sunlight, and partly for that more immersive feeling. The iPhone has long been my main camera, and with this DIY mod, I feel even more strongly that for a lot of situations, a phone is all you need.

Do you think this is a crazy idea or a stroke of genius? I'd love to hear what you think in the comments. If you think it's as useful as I do, unfortunately the version I bought appears to be discontinued, and I haven't found anything similar for screens larger than three inches yet. If you come across one, please drop a link in the comments.
